# `silk/bench/history`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The history of a benchmark suite: one line of text for each result of each run, the journal
a person keeps beside it, and the table that shows progress over time.

## When to use
Use [`History.lines`](#History.impl.lines) to add a run to a history file, and [`History.parse`](#History.impl.parse) with
[`History.terminal`](#History.impl.terminal) or [`History.markdown`](#History.impl.markdown) to show how a suite moved from run to run.
`silk.bench.bench` does both for a task: `--record` appends to
`bench/history/<suite>.jsonl`, and `--history` prints the table.

## Details
A history file is JSON Lines: each line is one [`Entry`](#Entry), the statistics of one
implementation on one benchmark in one run. Lines are only ever added, so the file diffs and
merges in a repository like any text. An entry holds no raw samples: those stay in the
result file of the run.

An entry carries the ratio to the reference measured in the same run. That ratio is the
steadiest number to follow over time, because both sides shared the computer and its noise.
Medians of two runs are compared only when both ran on the same computer, by
[`Entry.computer`](#Entry.computer): a change is called `faster` or `slower` when the 95% intervals of the two
medians do not overlap, and is a plain percentage otherwise.

The journal is a Markdown file a person writes, `bench/journal.md`: each `## ` heading is a
revision or a date, and the text under it says what changed there, such as "two-pass parse"
or "moved to a 4-core container". The table shows that text beside the first run of that
revision or date.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.history { Journal }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let text = run Journal.added("# Journal\n", "1503ff0", "two-pass parse")
  let notes = run Journal.parse(text.view())
  return match Journal.find(notes.asSlice(), "1503ff0") {
    Option<string>.Some { value } => if value == "two-pass parse" { 0 } else { 1 }
    Option<string>.None => 2
  }
}

effect fn failed(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 3
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `History` with `import silk.bench.history { History }`.

<a id="Journal.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(text: string) -> List<Note>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the sections of the journal `text`: one [`Note`](#Note) for each `## ` heading, with the
lines under it joined by spaces. Text before the first such heading is left out.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the notes.

<a id="Journal.impl.added"></a>

### Associated function `added`

```silk
pub effect fn added(text: string, key: string, entry: string) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the journal `text` with `entry` added under the heading `key`. When the last
heading of the journal is `key`, the entry joins its section; otherwise a new section
starts at the end.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="Journal.impl.find"></a>

### Associated function `find`

```silk
pub fn find<'notes>(notes: &'notes [Note], key: string) -> Option<string<'notes>>
```

Returns the text of the first section of `notes` whose heading is `key`, or whose heading
and `key` start alike when one is a shortened form of the other, as with a commit hash of
7 and of 40 characters. A shortened form has at least 7 characters.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the entries.

<a id="History.impl.lines"></a>

### Associated function `lines`

```silk
pub effect fn lines(report: &Report) -> String
    ! SchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the entries of `report` as the lines to add to a history file: one JSON object a
line, each line ended.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.
- `SchemaError` or `WriterError` if an entry cannot be encoded, which a value of a report
  that is not a finite number causes.

<a id="History.impl.bencher"></a>

### Associated function `bencher`

```silk
pub effect fn bencher(report: &Report) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns `report` in Bencher Metric Format, the JSON that the Bencher service reads: one
object whose keys are `<benchmark>/<implementation>`, each with one measure that holds
the median as `value` and its 95% interval as `lower_value` and `upper_value`.

#### Details
The measure is `latency` for a time, which Bencher takes in nanoseconds, and otherwise the
unit as the report has it, such as `req/s`. Rows with no successful run are left out.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="History.impl.drawn"></a>

### Associated function `drawn`

```silk
pub effect fn drawn(report: &mut Report, recorded: &[Entry]) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Gives every `history` chart of `report` its panels: one for each benchmark, with a line for
each implementation over the runs of `recorded` and then the run of `report` itself.

#### Details
A run is named by its revision, or by its day when it has none. A chart shows the entries
in its own unit, so a chart of a unit the history does not hold stays empty. A normalized
chart shows the ratio each entry recorded, when its reference is the chart's.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the panels.

<a id="History.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(text: string) -> List<Entry>
    ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError

```

Returns the entries of the history file `text`, in the order of its lines. Empty lines are
skipped.

#### Errors
- `SchemaError` if a line is not an entry.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the entries.

<a id="History.impl.terminal"></a>

### Associated function `terminal`

```silk
pub effect fn terminal(entries: &[Entry], notes: &[Note], color: bool) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the history `entries` as tables for a terminal: one for each implementation on
each benchmark, a row a run, oldest first. `notes` are the sections of the journal. With
`color`, the text holds ANSI escape codes.

#### Details
The columns are the date, the revision, the median, the change from the run before on the
same computer, the ratio to the reference of the same run, and the journal's text for the
revision or the day, shown at the first run that has it.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="History.impl.page"></a>

### Associated function `page`

```silk
pub effect fn page(suite: string, entries: &[Entry], notes: &[Note]) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the history `entries` of the suite `suite` as one static HTML page, in the style
of `silk.bench.html`: for each benchmark a chart over the runs, oldest first, and the
tables of [`History.terminal`](#History.impl.terminal).

#### Details
A chart draws one line for each implementation: its ratio to the reference of the same
run, with a dashed line at 1, or its median from zero when the benchmark has no ratio. A
dotted vertical line with a number marks the first run of a revision or a day the journal
has text for, and the text is listed under the chart.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="History.impl.markdown"></a>

### Associated function `markdown`

```silk
pub effect fn markdown(entries: &[Entry], notes: &[Note]) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError

```

Returns the history `entries` as Markdown: a heading and a table for each implementation
on each benchmark, with the columns of [`History.terminal`](#History.impl.terminal).

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.
